Improve performance in Playstation Portable version

Improve text positioning on all menus

Decrease the size of binary on all platforms

Log exceptions thanks to mardy on GitHub

name: GitHub Desktop
longDescription:
Focus on what matters instead of fighting with Git. Whether you're new to Git or a seasoned user, GitHub Desktop simplifies your development workflow.

Attribute commits with collaborators easily. Quickly add co-authors to your commit. Great for pairing and excellent for sending a little love/credit to that special someone who helped fix that gnarly bug of yours. See the attribution on the history page, undo an accidental attribution, and see the co-authors on github.com

Checkout branches with pull requests and view CI statuses. See all open pull requests for your repositories and check them out as if they were a local branch, even if they're from upstream branches or forks. See which pull requests pass commit status checks, too!]

Syntax highlighted diffs. The new GitHub Desktop supports syntax highlighting when viewing diffs for a variety of different languages.

Expanded image diff support. Easily compare changed images. See the before and after, swipe or fade between the two, or look at just the changed parts.

Extensive editor & shell integrations. Open your favorite editor or shell from the app, or jump back to GitHub Desktop from your shell. GitHub Desktop is your springboard for work.

Community supported. GitHub Desktop is open source now! Check out our roadmap, contribute, and help us make collaboration even easier.

This version of GitHub Desktop is a fork that adds support for Linux.
changelog:
Fixed

- Mitigates several vulnerabilities related to Git's credential helper protocol - CVE-2025-23040, CVE-2024-50349, CVE-2024-52006, CVE-2024-50338, CVE-2024-53263

name: PrimeHack
summary: Dolphin Emu fork for various Metroid Prime mods
longDescription: PrimeHack is a fork of Dolphin Emulator to bring modern Mouse and Keyboard controls, as well as Dual-Stick gamepad controls to the Metroid Prime Trilogy. PrimeHack also offers many other features such as increased FoV and various new cheats.

name: SHM Modbus
summary: Tools to simulate a Modbus client
longDescription:
Contains the following tools:

- dump-shm
- write-shm
- shared-mem-random
- modbus-tcp-client-shm
- modbus-rtu-client-shm
- stdin-to-modbus-shm
- shm-modbus-signal-gen
- shm-modbus-gui
- wago-modbus-coupler-shm
- shm-format

name: Brief
longDescription:
Brief is an app for browsing command-line cheatsheets. It lets you search through thousands of command-line tools across multiple platforms and languages, providing simplified help pages.

Features:

- Works completely offline.
- Fuzzy search through the available commands.
- Filter platform specific commands (Linux, Windows, Android, etc.).
- View command help pages in multiple available languages.
- Change the command argument format between long (`ls --all`) or short (`ls -a`).
- Lets you update the cache within the app to download the latest data.
changelog:
Release 0.3.2

- Fix app icon black background issue in KDE
- Update deps

name: Defuse
longDescription:
Defuse let's you remove background from photos locally.

Features:

- Images are processed locally
- Uses WebGPU acceleration on x86_64 systems
changelog:
Release v0.1.3

- Implement image drag and drop
- Add image loading visuals
- Fix images not displaying for some formats (webp, avif, etc.)

name: Exchange
longDescription:
Exchange lets you convert between GTK UI definition formats such as XML and Blueprint.

Features:

- Convert XML to Blueprint
- Convert Blueprint to XML
- Automatically detects format when pasting or opening files
changelog:
Release 0.2.2

- Change to app icon designed by bda-git

name: Lipi
longDescription:
Discover and install thousands of fonts directly on your system with Lipi.

Features:

- Preview fonts offline without needing to install them.
- Test fonts with your own custom text to see how they look.
- Search through categories like Sans, Serif, and Monospace.
- Quickly install the latest fonts to your system.
- View font details, including the designer, license, and file info.
- High-quality fonts sourced directly from the Google Fonts GitHub repository.
changelog:
Release v0.3.1

- Change to app icon designed by Jakub Steiner

name: Spruce
longDescription:
Spruce is a lightweight cache cleaner and system maintenance tool designed for GNU/Linux. It helps keep your system fresh by clearing unneeded caches, logs, and temporary files in a clean, Adwaita-based GTK interface.

- Scan common cache locations
- Detect unused Flatpak runtimes and data
- Preview exactly what will be removed
- Clean with a single click
changelog:
- Pie chart now shows cache and trash separately
- Preferences are now saved between sessions
- Fixed a memory leak with the preferences menu

name: QDirStat
longDescription:
QDirStat is a graphical application to show where your disk space has gone and to help you to clean it up.

It shows the total size of directories and of their files both in a traditional tree view and in a colored treemap graphics where a large file is shown as a large rectangle, and small files are shown as small rectangles. Click on it, and you will see where in the tree the file is, and you can instantly move it to the trash if you like. The color corresponds to the file type: Images, videos or whatever.

name: VirtAudio
summary: Create virtual microphones from browser audio
longDescription: VirtAudio allows you to create virtual microphones from browser audio sources. It enables you to capture and route audio from web browsers to other applications through virtual microphone devices.
changelog: Initial release of VirtAudio

name: Ping Monitor
longDescription:
Ping Monitor is a simple tool to monitor your network.

Features:

- Display your ping in real time as a nice chart
- Make it obvious when you're disconnected
- Monitor download and upload speeds
- Display local and public IP addresses
- Automatically detect network and VPN changes
changelog: Handle timeouts correctly

name: Record Apps
longDescription: Record Apps is a simple application that allows you to record audio from individual applications. It uses PipeWire to capture the audio output of each application separately.
changelog:
- Use pipewire api for media name (more reliable)
- Add app-level pinning with Auto-Record and Auto-Listen
- Group media by apps
- Rename Listen/Mute button to Monitor with speaker icons

name: Share
longDescription:
Share is a bidirectional file sharing application that works both ways — send files to others or receive files from them. It offers both a graphical interface (GTK) and a terminal-based CLI mode.

Features:

How it works:

Perfect for quick file transfers between devices, mobile-to-desktop uploads, collaborative work, or any situation where you need wireless file transfer without cloud services.

- Bidirectional file transfer - both send and receive files
- No additional software required - just a QR code scanner and web browser
- Receive Mode - let others upload files directly to your device
- Directory uploads - upload/download entire folder structures
- Multiple file uploads - batch upload many files at once
- Share data from the clipboard, automatically detect if the clipboard contains an image, or a text, note that pasting files will only send paths as text (if the app doesn't have read permission), so its better to drop them instead
- CLI mode — run entirely from the terminal without a graphical interface, useful over SSH or on headless systems
- Creates a temporary HTTP server on your local network
- Generates QR codes for both sharing and receiving
- Sharing Mode: Others scan to download your files
- Receive Mode: Others scan to upload files to you via web interface
- All transfers happen locally over your network - no internet required
changelog: - Better local ip detection, show more local interfaces

name: Stimulator
longDescription:
Prevents the desktop environment (DE) from sleeping. It should work regardless of the used DE thanks to the Inhibit portal.

Features:

- Overrides system setting and disables automatic suspending
- Overrides system setting and disables screen blanking and screen locking
- Option to use system default, light or dark theme
- AppIndicator support
changelog: - Port to JS GTK (native js gtk bidings, drop python bridge)

name: Signus: The Artefact Wars
longDescription:
Signus is a Czech turn-based strategy game from 1998, developed by Valacirca and released by Zima Software. Since 2002 it is free and open source software with both code and assets.

The game features 40 units: scout vehicles, tanks, artillery, helicopters, planes, ships, and support units providing repairs, refuels and ammo. There are also nine buildings and five defense towers in the game.

name: Squeeze Vid
summary: Normalize videos to a minimal, projection-compatible quality.
longDescription: Normalize videos and audio files (using ffmpeg) to a standardized frame rate and quality to minimize the file size while maintaining adequate quality for video projection.
changelog: Flatpak-ready release.

name: Marca
summary: Find saved websites & app deeplinks quickly using powerful tagging and full-text search
longDescription:
Marca's a URL manager. It treats everything as tags: tags themselves, hierarchy (akin to folders), whether a bookmark is trashed, uncategorized, etc. All this, + inclusive/exclusive filtering is available through the sidebar.

Features:

- Full-Text Search
- Filter using tags inclusively/exclusively
- Sort by created, modified, title, URL, Relevance
- Keyboard controls
- Import/export to JSON/HTML
- Coming soon: cloud-free sync, reader mode and more.
changelog:
New:

Bug fixes:

- Sidebar redesigned: hotkey hint for tag search, special tags are now always visible
- Orphan tags get deleted on hard delete
- New Sepia theme for easy readability in upcoming reader mode
- Add bookmark from highlighted text with --add-selection - pair it with a keyboard shortcut!
- Deleted bookmarks get restored and updated when their url is added
- Orphan tags get deleted on hard delete

name: Black Chocobo
summary: Save editor for Final Fantasy VII
longDescription:
Supports saves from the PC98, Steam, PC2012, Playstation, Uncompressed Virtual Memory Card Formats, PS3, PSP, PsVita, and Switch Versions of Final Fantasy 7. Black Chocobo is a powerful editor with many features. In addtion to standard save editing there are many additonal convenience features. One Example would be the abliity to convert your save to another format so you can continue your adventue on a different platform. Another example is the "New Game + feature.

This Application requests full system read and write access in order to write to removable media such as USB sticks. It is also needed to write into the Final Fantasy 7 save path if it is not installed inside your home folder. Removing access in your flatpak application settings will not break the applicaion but you will restrict where you are able to read and save your edited files.
changelog:
This stable Release fixes a few bugs and a possible application crashes.

- Fix: Crash when exporting a character
- Fix: missing translations
- Fix: Non english item searching
- Update to ff7tk 1.2.0

name: Sitra
longDescription:
Get your fonts from online sources with a sleek, friendly user interface. Sitra provides a seamless experience for installing, uninstalling and previewing fonts.

- List fonts available on Google Fonts
- Preview the fonts using Fontsource CDN for privacy
- Get code to use the font in your project, via CDN or npm from fontsource
- Download the fonts on your device in ttf format from google
- Filter font by category using the toggle buttons or by family and subset using search
changelog:
- Added Turkish translations
- Added a badge to installed fonts
- Sort installed fonts first

name: Safe Eyes
summary: A FOSS tool for Linux users to reduce and prevent repetitive strain injury (RSI)
longDescription:
Protect your eyes from eye strain using this simple and beautiful, yet extensible break reminder

Features:

Remind you to take breaks with exercises to reduce RSI, Disable keyboard during breaks, Notification before and after breaks, Smart pause if system is idle, Multi-screen support, Customizable user interface, Command-line arguments to control the running instance, Customizable using plug-ins
changelog: break fade-in, bugfix for running from source and missing breaks, updated translations

name: SmallBASIC
longDescription: SmallBASIC is a fast and easy to learn BASIC language interpreter ideal for everyday calculations, scripts and prototypes. Includes support for modules: raylib, nuklear, websocket, glfw, clipboard
changelog: Resolved an issue when returning from the online screen

name: Space Nerds in Space
longDescription:
Space Nerds In Space is an open source (GPLv2) cooperative multiplayer starship simulator for linux. So go out and get together with a crew of your linux-nerd friends and their computers in a room with a projector or TV, and go forth and explore the galaxy.

Space Nerds In Space allows you to man the various bridge controls of a starship. You can play Space Nerds In Space alone or with friends, but you really need a crew of 2 or more players to master a starship.

Various stations are Captain (Main Screen), Helms, Weapons, Communications, Science/Scanning, and Engineering/Repair.

Note that unlike many other fine bridge simulators, Space Nerds In Space is fully 3D.

Space Nerds In Space also has an option where someone can take the role of dungeon master and modify the game universe in progress.

There are warp gates, nebula that block sensors and allow you to hide, mining, courier missions, and of course many hostiles. Creating your own scriptable missions in lua is possible and encouraged. And much, much more.

name: Progress
longDescription: Whether you’re a software developer, a project manager, or simply someone who enjoys keeping track of personal goals, Progress gives you the essential framework to organize tasks effectively while also being simple and easy to use.
changelog:
What's new in Progress 1.7.3

This patch release includes minor style changes and behavior enhancements.

- The cards menu buttons are consistent with all the menu buttons in the application
- Color radio button group implementation has been refactored

name: zelda3
summary: Zelda3 is a reverse engineered clone of Zelda - A Link to the Past
longDescription:
Zelda3 is a reverse engineered clone of Zelda - A Link to the Past.

A bunch of features have been added that are not supported by the original game.

SHA1: 6d4f10a8b10e10dbe624cb23cf03b88bb8252973

In addition, translations can be added through localized ROMs.

name: Khushu
summary: An all-in-one Muslim app for Linux
longDescription:
Khushu is your all-in-one Muslim app for Linux desktop, tablets, and smartphones. It centralizes your daily worship by providing accurate prayer times, native staggered Adkar notifications, and a dedicated Noble Quran reader with ayah-by-ayah recitation.

- Accurate offline prayer (Salah) calculation methods, including recommended high-latitude and polar estimation methods.
- Morning, Evening, and Night Adkar with built-in counters
- Customizable Adhan system notifications (Makkah/Madinah audio)
- Dedicated Noble Quran reader with authentic Uthmanic text, multi-language translations, ayah-by-ayah recitation, selectable reciters, and adjustable typography
- Interactive Qibla compass
- Hijri calendar mapping
- Privacy-first local encryption for your location data
- Modern Libadwaita interface with adaptive Dark Mode
- Multi-language support
changelog:
- Added per-mode location stores for Manual, City, and Auto
- Added tooltips for Quran recitation controls
- Fixed next-prayer lookup returning past prayers
- Fixed stale iqamah countdown after a location change
- Updated prayer calculation library to mawaqit 0.4

name: godl
longDescription: Manage your Godot projects and versions in one place. Features include: - Editor version bindings to projects that transfer across source control - Download versions of forks of Godot as well - Rich CLI for automation - Qt UI, good for KDE Plasma
changelog: Release v1.3 brings some new features and bugfixes!

name: Qobine
longDescription:
Listening to your Qobuz music with Qobine: a Qobuz client designed for GNOME.

Upon first launch, a browser spawns where you will need to login to Qobuz with your active streaming subscription.

Qobine supports full Qobuz audio quality. But make sure that your pipewire configuration is correct.

- View and stream your favorite albums, artists and playlists
- Search the full Qobuz catalogue
- Add / remove favorites
- Add to queue / play next
- Create / edit / delete playlists
changelog: Added discover page

name: WebCord
longDescription:
This flatpak is not supported by webcord directly! Please open issues on the flathub repository first!

An Electron wrapper for the Discord web-client. It introduces new privacy features and an optionnal native wayland support.

name: SRB2 Reveries
summary: Gameplay overhaul mod for Sonic Robo Blast 2
longDescription: Sonic Robo Blast 2 is a 3D open-source Sonic the Hedgehog fangame built using the Doom Legacy port of Doom. Reveries is one of the two main flavours of the SRB2 Cherry project, featuring heavy modifications to more closely recreate the gameplay seen in the classic games SRB2 was inspired by on top of the SRB2 Cherry base which adds fixes and other quality of life features such as the shield button and improved gamepad support.

name: Pulse
summary: Local-first burnout and energy tracking for GNOME
longDescription:
Pulse helps you log energy levels, spot recovery patterns, review weekly burnout signals, and keep lightweight rituals on a private local database.

The app is built for GNOME with GTK 4 and Libadwaita and is designed to stay responsive on narrow and wide window sizes.

name: Diurnals
longDescription:
Not keeping up with upcoming and overdue tasks? Better track your tasks on Todoist with a popup that appears regularly.

Features:

Note: Diurnals is not affiliated with or created by Doist

- Customizable popup times
- Apply custom filters for tasks
- Manage your tasks and your time more efficiently

name: Stella
longDescription:
The Atari 2600 Video Computer System (VCS), introduced in 1977, was the most popular home video game system of the early 1980's. Now you can enjoy all of your favorite Atari 2600 games on your PC thanks to Stella!

Stella is a multi-platform Atari 2600 VCS emulator released under the GNU General Public License (GPL). Stella was originally developed for Linux by Bradford W. Mott, and is currently maintained by Stephen Anthony. Since its original release several people have joined the development team to port Stella to other operating systems such as AcornOS, AmigaOS, DOS, FreeBSD, IRIX, Linux, OS/2, MacOS, Unix, and Windows. The development team is working hard to perfect the emulator and we hope you enjoy our effort.

name: Katalog
longDescription:
Catalog your devices to search, analyze, and backup your files:

- Create catalogs from different devices, including metadata or checksums
- Search and explore files even when the devices are disconnected
- Search with advanced filters using including metadata or checksums, and find duplicates or differences
- Organize your collection of devices and files, and get statistics
- Backup or Archive files between catalogs
- Multiple language support, OpenSource, Cross-platform (Linux, Windows, macOS)
changelog: Search list, Search Regex, Catalog split

name: chiaki-ng
summary: Free and Open Source Client for PlayStation Remote Play
longDescription: chiaki-ng is the next-generation of Chiaki, adding new features and ongoing support as the original project (Chiaki) is in maintenance mode. It is a free and Open Source Client for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 Remote Play. It can be used to play in real time on a PlayStation as long as there is a network connection.
changelog:
This release provides the following improvements:

- improve streaming quality and stability with better queueing, reset handling, congestion control, and streaming metrics
- add an OpenGL renderer backend plus major renderer and libplacebo fixes, adaptive queue depth, and custom upscalers
- add VSync support plus spatial upscaler presets under settings->video->Render
- improve PSN remote play reliability with configurable NAT port guessing and holepunching fixes
- rework audio, microphone, and haptics paths for better recovery and fewer failure cases
- fix macOS ARM rendering, crash-on-exit, and controller input issues, and add iOS/tvOS compilation support

name: Ymir
longDescription:
Ymir is a work-in-progress Sega Saturn emulator. Ymir includes the following features:

- Load games from MAME CHD, BIN+CUE, IMG+CCD, MDF+MDS or ISO files
- Automatic IPL (BIOS) ROM detection
- Automatic region switching
- Up to two players with a variety of controllers on both ports
- Fully customizable keybindings
- Backup RAM, DRAM and ROM cartridges (more to come)
- Integrated backup memory manager to import and export saves, and transfer between internal and cartridge RAM
- Forwards-compatible save states
- Rewinding (up to one minute at 60 fps), turbo speed, frame step (forwards and backwards)
- Full screen mode with VRR support and low input lag
- Graphics enhancements such as optional deinterlaced/progressive rendering of high resolution modes and transparent mesh polygon rendering
- Optional low level CD block emulation
- A work-in-progress feature-rich debugger

name: Muon
summary: Graphical SFTP client and terminal emulator with helpful utilities
longDescription: Muon is a graphical SSH client. It has a enhanced SFTP file browser, SSH terminal emulator, remote resource/process manager, server disk space analyzer, remote text editor, huge remote log viewer and lots of other helpful tools, which makes it easy to work with remote servers. Muon provides functionality similar to web based control panels but, it works over SSH from local computer, hence no installation required on server. It runs on Linux and Windows. Muon has been tested with serveral Linux and UNIX servers, like Ubuntu server, CentOS, RHEL, OpenSUSE, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD and HP-UX.
changelog:
- Fixed multiple password prompt and focus issue.
- Added re-arrange via drag drop of connections in connection manager
- Import sessions from Putty and WinScp
- Configurable initial tab
- Fixed text editor and terminal focus issue.
- Added HTTP, Socks4 and Socks5 proxy.
- Several minor bugfixes.

name: Subsound
summary: Stream music from your Navidrome Server
longDescription:
Subsound is a GTK4/Adwaita music player for Subsonic-compatible streaming servers, with Navidrome as the primary target. It lets you browse artists, albums, and playlists from your personal music server and plays them back directly or from a local cache.

Features include:

For offline mode, remember to first Sync Library.

- Browse and play music from Navidrome or any Subsonic-compatible server
- Playlist management
- Starred songs and downloaded songs views
- Offline playback from a local song cache
- Offline first scrobble back to server
- MPRIS media player integration for desktop media controls
- Native GTK4/Adwaita interface designed for GNOME
changelog:
- New: normalize playback loudness with ReplayGain so tracks and albums play at an even volume
- New: drag songs onto a playlist in the playlists overview to add them
- New: update bindings to be based on gnome 50

name: Tangent
longDescription:
Tangent lets you write the way you think. Your thoughts are connected; Tangent lets you link to existing notes and make new ones with ease. Let your mind wander along the path of interest. Don't suppress tangential thoughts; embrace them. Key features include:

Tangent reads and writes plaintext notes using a loose interpretation of Markdown syntax. Text is rendered in a pseudo-WYSIWYG style, with formatting characters appearing only when you need them. Tangent supports bold, italics, headers, lists, links, images, todos, tags, inline code, block code with syntax highlighting, inline and block KaTeX math, color highlights, strikethrough, and comments.

- [[Wiki-link]] linking to other files in your workspace by name.
- Horizontally-scrolling sliding panels for quickly moving back and forth along a trail of thoughts.
- A Map View of the links between notes created and followed during your current session.
- Note creation automation with support for creating notes within folders defined by wildcards.
- Full-workspace note search powered by a custom query language.
changelog:
- Added commands for activating color highlights. They are now accessible from the application and context menus and can have keyboard shortcuts bound to them.
- Added a command for toggling checkboxes on and off (Ctrl+[).

changelog:
Version 0.21.5 - terminals that follow the desktop's appearance, a notification for a finished command, and packages that finally build what they can:

- Terminal colours can now follow the desktop's light or dark preference, through a new Follow System theme. Until now the System colour scheme reached only the window, so a light desktop could surround a dark terminal with no setting that paired them — and they now stay paired when the desktop switches while sessions are open
- A new monitoring mode notifies you when a command finishes on the remote host, with its exit code, so "finished" and "failed with status 1" are different messages. The existing modes guess from output timing; this one reads an event the shell reports. It needs shell integration on the remote host
- Every monitoring notification now leaves a mark on the tab until you look at it, visible in the tab bar and on the Tab Overview thumbnail
- Fixed: the window rendered light on a dark desktop whenever the theme was set to System
- Fixed: the Flatpak could not reach the new command notification at all, and the packages built for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE and macOS were quietly built against an older libadwaita than the one installed — in the Debian and Ubuntu case also without the in-tab browser. Every channel now asks what the system actually provides
- Fixed: the .deb and .rpm attached to a GitHub release did not list every library the program loads, so the .deb installed and then refused to start with "error while loading shared libraries". Both now derive that list from the binary instead of carrying one written by hand
- Fixed: every tray menu item that opens a session did nothing — Local Shell, Quick Connect and all of Recent Connections. The item highlighted on click and then nothing happened, on the KDE tray and on macOS alike
- Fixed: five icons drew as broken placeholders, because the icon theme had dropped the names they asked for. One of them was the mark shown when a command finishes, on the very notification the new mode exists to deliver
- Fixed: with the interface in any language other than English, KeePassXC was reported as unreadable when the database was open and healthy, and a password stored in the encrypted file became unreachable as a result
- Fixed: local shell tabs were never monitored, in any mode, so the new command notification could not fire on one
- Fixed: the monitoring bar's margins had never been applied, because they were spelled with property names GTK's CSS does not have

Ungoogled Chromium retains the default Chromium experience as closely as possible. Unlike other Chromium forks that have their own visions of a web browser, Ungoogled Chromium is essentially a drop-in replacement for Chromium.

Without signing in to a Google Account, Chromium does pretty well in terms of security and privacy. However, Chromium still has some dependency on Google web services and binaries. In addition, Google designed Chromium to be easy and intuitive for users, which means they compromise on transparency and control of inner operations.

Ungoogled Chromium addresses these issues in the following ways:

These features are implemented as configuration flags, patches, and custom scripts.

- Remove all remaining background requests to any web services while building and running the browser
- Remove all code specific to Google web services
- Remove all uses of pre-made binaries from the source code, and replace them with user-provided alternatives when possible
- Disable features that inhibit control and transparency, and add or modify features that promote them (these changes will almost always require manual activation or enabling)

name: Constrict
longDescription:
Constrict compresses your videos to your chosen file size — useful for uploading to services with specific file size limits. No more relying on online services for video compression, or the manual trial-and-error of re-encoding at various bitrates yourself.

Features include:

The app attempts to retain as much audiovisual quality as possible for the file size given. However, extremely steep reductions in file size can cause significant loss of quality in the output file, and sometimes compression may not be possible at all. All processing is done locally — and as such, compression speeds are only as fast as your hardware allows.

- An intuitive, easy to use interface.
- Automatic calculation of average bitrate (ABR), resolution, framerate, and audio quality each video is re-encoded with to meet the target file size.
- Bulk compression of multiple videos to one output directory.
- Customization of framerate limits, to ensure a clearer or smoother image.
- A choice of codecs to encode output files with, including H.264, HEVC, AV1, and VP9.
changelog:
- Exported videos now support mono audio, if the input was also in mono.
- Improved audio quality on heavy compressions.
- Fixed a crash caused by videos having odd widths or heights.
- Opening a compressed video in the file manager should now open in its 'real' directory; not the Flatpak sandboxed directory.
- Video source warnings will now correctly show after cancelling a compression.
- When a video compresses to under the file size limit outside the tolerance, it'll no longer fail if the number of compression attempts for that video is greater than 1. This is to save time, and prevent infinite attempts with exponentially increasing bitrates, which eventually cause an error.

name: Gitpulsar
summary: Fast native Git client for GNOME
longDescription:
Gitpulsar is a complete Git client built natively for GNOME. Written in Rust with GTK4 and libadwaita, it stays fast and lightweight while giving you the full Git workflow without ever leaving the keyboard or reaching for the terminal.

Unlike browser-wrapped Git apps, Gitpulsar is a single small binary that follows your system theme, respects your accent color preferences, and feels like a first-class GNOME application. It runs offline, sends nothing to the cloud, and uses zero telemetry.

Why choose Gitpulsar:

What you can do:

- Native GNOME look and feel — libadwaita widgets, dark and light themes, dynamic colors
- Multi-repository workspace — open a folder, see all repos with live status indicators (modified, untracked, ahead of remote)
- Adaptive layout — works from a 4K monitor down to a 360 px phone screen (Phosh, postmarketOS)
- Low CPU and memory — Rust core with smart background polling that pauses when the window isn't focused
- No telemetry, no account, no cloud — your code stays on your machine
- Browse history with a paginated commit log, search, and an integrated branch graph
- Stage and unstage by file, by hunk, or by individual line — with drag and drop
- Commit with conventional commit prefixes (feat, fix, docs…) and one-click Co-Authored-By trailers
- Undo and redo staging operations and even file discards
- Resolve merge conflicts in a three-panel visual editor
- Run interactive rebase with reorder, squash, fixup, reword, edit, and drop actions
- Annotate any file with blame to see who changed each line
- View per-file commit history to debug regressions
- Clone a repository from a URL with a built-in dialog
- Manage remotes — add, rename, remove, and edit URLs
- Push and delete tags on the remote, create lightweight or annotated tags
- Export commits as patches and apply patches with git am or git apply
- Browse the reflog to recover from accidental reset, rebase, or branch operations
- Manage stashes, submodules, and worktrees from the sidebar
- Edit .gitignore inside the app
- Use the full keyboard — shortcuts for every common action and Tab-cycling across panels

name: LibreWolf

LibreWolf is NOT associated with Mozilla or its products.

Features:

- Latest Version of Firefox: LibreWolf is compiled directly from the latest build of Firefox Stable. You will have the the latest features, and security updates.
- Completely Independent Build: LibreWolf uses a completely independent build from Firefox and has its own settings, profile folder and installation path. As a result, it can be installed alongside Firefox or any other browser.
- Settings protection: important settings are enforced/locked within librewolf.cfg and policies.json, those settings cannot be changed by addons/updates/LibreWolf itself or unwanted/accidental manipulation; To change those settings you can easily do it by editing librewolf.cfg and policies.json.
- LibreWolf-addons: set of optional LibreWolf extensions
- Statistics disabled: telemetry and similar functions are disabled
- Tested settings: settings are performance aware
- Recommended and code reviewed addons list
- Community-Driven
- And much more…

longDescription:
VoiceGen is a simple piece of software for reading your texts. It can give you a limited access to Streamlabs (amazon polly) voices, also it provides an interface followed by an enhancer for svox pico text to speech engine.

It can be used as a text reader or a narrator for your project/video.

Features:

With ❤ by PersianGolf

- Easy to use and minimal
- Save output files
- Multiple speech engines
- Voice enhancer for svox
changelog:
C++26 and Qt6

- Parts of the code base has been re-written for Qt6
- Moved to C++26 and its hardening features for memory-safety
- Bugfixes and interface improvements

name: USB Imager
summary: Write many USB drives at once
longDescription:
USB-Imager writes a disk image to several USB drives at the same time. Connected drives are detected automatically.

Drive access is handled by the udisks2 service of the system. Entering a password is only required for writing when the policy of the distribution in use demands it.

Before writing, the image can be checked against a checksum. After writing, it is possible to verify the content of the drives.

Features:

- Writing an image to multiple USB drives at once
- Automatic drive detection
- Fast writing through the sendfile() system call
- Adjustable write buffer between 1 MiB and 4 MiB
- Optional validation of the written image
- Optional checksum verification of the selected image
- Automatic unmounting of the drives
- Warning for ISO files that do not look bootable
- Statistics about writing time and overall speed
- Selectable color scheme (Auto, Light, Dark)
changelog:
- The Flatpak package now needs considerably less storage space. The installation size was reduced from about 278 MiB to 19 MiB, without limiting what the program can do.
- The Open dialog now uses the file dialog of the desktop. It therefore looks different from before, but still gives access to all folders.
- The Flathub page of USB-Imager is now fully translated into English, German and French. Other languages are no longer offered.
- In the application menu the program is now shown as "USB Imager" without the hyphen.
- The Flathub page now shows four screenshots instead of just one, among them the dark color scheme. Its own colors and a shorter description were also added.
- A crash in the Flatpak package was fixed. Previously, closing a window such as "About" with the button in its title bar could crash the whole application.

name: Stone Kingdoms
longDescription: Experience the thrill of medieval castle building and destruction in our isometric, open source strategy game - a modern remake of Firefly Studios' classic Stronghold. Immerse yourself in a world of strategy and tactical decision making as you design and defend your own castles in medieval Europe.
changelog:
Bug fix release:

- Fixed moonwalking peasants at campfire.
- Fixed freeze before loading or exiting game.
- Fixed crash when loading a game with placed stone gates.
- Added Grasslands map for testing purposes.
- Added partial Hungarian translations.
- and more!

name: Upscaler
longDescription: Upscaler enhances and enlarges images up to four times their original size, with special modes for cartoons, anime and photos.
changelog:
- Add Cornish (Kernewek) translation
- Fix a bug where dragging an image while a dialog is open would cause the drop overlay to not unapply until the dialog is closed again

name: Jollpi
longDescription:
Jollpi is a lightweight text editor focused on simplicity and native GTK integration.

The application applies a custom GTK styling to maintain a consistent visual appearance across different environments.

Key features:

- Modern GTK4-based interface
- Syntax highlighting for many programming and markup languages
- Multi-tab and multi-window editing for working with multiple files
- Find & Replace, Go to Line, and fast navigation tools
- Automatic file change detection and reload
- Customizable fonts, themes, and wrap mode
- Mini map, line numbers, auto-bracket and auto-indent
changelog:
- Fixed memory leak when closing the last remaining tab
- Fixed stale GLib source ID warning when removing already-executed timeouts
- Auto-fill search entry with selected text on selection and when opening find bar
- Simplified navbar reference passing across window, notebook, and menu
- Fixed light/dark branding colors being swapped in metainfo.xml

name: Munquet
longDescription:
Munquet is a lightweight desktop tool for converting and preparing tabular data files with ease.

Transform structured data into the efficient Apache Parquet format, reduce file size, merge datasets, and validate column structures — all through a simple graphical interface.

Key features:

- Convert CSV/TSV files to Parquet
- Merge multiple datasets into one
- Validate and rename column headers safely
- Prevent inconsistent or mismatched data
- Batch processing with progress feedback
- Works fully offline
changelog: - Resolve portal paths to host paths in error details

name: GPT4ALL
longDescription:
Cross platform Qt based GUI for GPT4All

- Fast CPU and GPU based inference using ggml for open source LLM's
- The UI is made to look and feel like you've come to expect from a chatty gpt
- Check for updates so you can always stay fresh with latest models
- Easy to install with precompiled binaries available for all three major desktop platforms
- Multi-model - Ability to load more than one model and switch between them
- Supports llama.cpp style models
- Model downloader in GUI featuring many popular open source models
- Settings dialog to change temp, top_p, top_k, threads, etc
- Copy your conversation to clipboard

name: Greenery
longDescription: The First Cryptocurrency Wallet with Bookkeeping and Accounting Functionality in mind for Avid traders, Small Business owners and Accountants
changelog:
- Signup using an email/password and a custom or generated 12 word mnemonic phrase
- Create a GreeneryID to share with up to 8 wallet addresses attached
- Easily import contacts/addresses using a shared GreeneryID
- Keep track of your assets using an easy to read portfolio page
- View indicies PoW, PoS, Coinbase (NY), Gemini (NY), and Storage
- Generate up to 5 wallets at a time using your mnemonic phrase
- Generate unlimited throwaway wallets

- Send crypto using a public address, stored contact, or human readable domains (Unstoppable, ENS, Tezos Domains)

- Easily swap your crypto for another using our quick exchange with expanded currency support

- Generate paper wallets for personal storage

- Export and import contacts using drag and drop for CSV and VCF files

name: Howl
summary: Lightweight editor with keyboard-centric minimalistic interface
longDescription: Howl is a general purpose editor that aims to be both lightweight and fully customizable. It is built on top of the very fast LuaJIT runtime, and can be extended in either Lua or Moonscript. It has a minimalistic UI driven mainly by the keyboard.

name: HTTPie
summary: Cross-platform API testing client for humans
longDescription:
HTTPie Desktop is a cross-platform API testing client for humans. It offers all the user-friendliness of the terminal version of httpie, now wrapped up in a sleek graphical interface.

- Interact painlessly with APIs
- Leverage the power of AI-assisted work
- Organize your work in spaces, collections, and tabs
- Parametrize requests with variables and environments
- Work across devices with auto-save and realtime sync
- Build and preview requests without sending them
- Use the app offline and without an account
changelog:
✨ Enhancements

- 📤 Export/Import — Backup, share, or publish your data as JSON.
- 🗂️ Export a whole space — Transfer entire workspaces with all content.
- 🔒 Export private items — Include drafts and local environments in exports.
- 📂 Collection export — Share and back up request collections.
- 🛫 Request export — Export with optional auth and variable embedding.
- 🌍 Environment export — Share variables across teams and projects.

- 📋 Copy as — Instantly generate CLI commands from requests.
- 🔗 Path parameters — Parametrize URLs with /:param syntax.
- ✨ Other enhancements — Fixed Postman import, etc.

name: The AMC Squad
summary: Epic story-driven FPS running on the Build Engine
longDescription:
The AMC Squad is an epic story-driven FPS running on the Build Engine. It combines gameplay mechanics of retro-shooters with aspects of modern titles, complete with a story-driven narrative that spans over several episodes.

Each episode is a full-length campaign featuring multiple varied locations to explore and many hidden secrets and collectibles to discover. Experience an overarching story that is loosely based on the worlds and settings of other classic Build Engine games. Pick from more than 8 different characters, each with a unique set of items, weapons and abilities, and fight a large selection of different enemy factions that threaten the safety of the world.

The game currently contains 4 fully playable episodes, with 6 episodes planned total. Episode 5 is currently in development. No release date estimate is available at this time.

Features:

- Classic FPS gameplay mixed with modern mechanics.
- Mission-based level structure, spanning 4+ separate episodes, with more than 20 hours worth of content.
- Intricate and highly interactive levels, with many secrets to find.
- A rich story consisting of multiple character arcs and plot threads.
- 8 different characters with different gameplay styles, with more to unlock as you progress.
- Unique loadout of weapons and items for each character, as well as level-specific weapons to find and unlock.
- Collectibles, weapon replacements and a fully-fledged progress system.
- Upgradeable weapons and character abilities.
- Multiple vehicles, including motorcycles, spaceships, tanks and horses.
- In-game cutscenes and pre-rendered FMV sequences, complete with voice acting and subtitles.
- Original music composed by HiveBoss, TheDavisD, AliCatGamer, and various tracks sourced from OpenGameArt.
- And more features you never thought possible in a Build Engine game!

name: Laigter
summary: Tool to generate normal, specular, occlussion and parallax maps for 2D textures
longDescription: Laigter is a tool that automatically generates maps for dynamic lighting effects in games. It allows normal, parallax, specular and occlusion map generation. Also, it allows the user to preview how the effect will look ingame.

name: Skippy The Bot
summary: Skippy is on an epic quest to unravel its true destiny
longDescription:
This game was made to celebrate AM2R's 5th anniversary, and it's based on a brief sequence where you remotely control a robot. In this puzzle physics platformer, you'll be challenged to complete 30 hand crafted levels. It's a short experience, that makes it very appealing to try speed running, or other challenges:

Have fun!

- Can you complete the game while collecting all the gems?
- Can you complete the game without collecting any gems at all?
- How about a deathless run?

name: Domestique Baston
longDescription:
Domestique Baston is a 1 vs 1 fighting game. Well. You know what that is... It’s intended for casual gamers as the gameplay is simple...

It pictures a couple fighting each other at home. That’s the reason why there is only 1 background and 2 playable characters.

This game is in French slang just because it’s funny. No other reason. Besides, who really cares about, for instance, the story or even what’s told in such a game?

- Use Alt-Enter to enter/exit full screen mode.
- When playing with a keyboard, the LEFT player uses the E, S, R, D keys for buttons, and the F, C, V, B keys for moving; the RIGHT player uses the O, K, P, L keys for buttons, and the arrow keys for moving.
- do notWe strongly recommend youplay on a keyboard as there are "ghosting" issues (some key combinations do not work).

name: Java Jolt!
longDescription:
Java Jolt! is a point & click adventure game where your morning caffeine fix is a matter of survival. Play as Rowena Pitifool, a copywriter who must find a way to get her coffee while enduring the relentless jabs of a particularly annoying inner voice.

Explore, combine, and improvise to salvage your day before it descends into chaos.

name: Kindergarten Massaker
summary: An alien lands in a kindergarten where the children quickly turn hostile
longDescription:
A peaceful alien lands in a kindergarten. Kids are coming from everywhere. More and more. They surround the alien, and they want blood! The alien has to avoid kids in order to survive. Everything is seen through a surveillance cam that gets buggier and buggier until it shuts down completely. End of game?

This (non) shooter game is in German, as we all know that aliens only speak German. So, deal with it!

name: itch
summary: Install, update and play indie games
longDescription:
The itch.io app, itch, lets you effortlessly download and run games and software from itch.io. All of your downloads are kept in a single place and are automatically updated. Access your collections and purchases, or browse for new games via the in-app browser.

Browse games like the creator intended.

Always updated.

Browser games offline.

Join the community.

Available in your language.

- On itch.io creators control how their project pages look. The built in browser lets you download and install games while exploring the unique page designs of our creators.
- Not only will the games you've installed automatically update, the app itself will automatically transform as we launch new functionality and features. Games using our new command line tools will generate delta patches, ensuring that you only download what's changed when new games come out.
- You can sync any browser based games right into the app, letting you play them offline whenever you want. Once you're back online you'll be able to grab any updates if necessary.
- Learn more about the development of the app in our community. Share feature requests and general feedback with other members of itch.io. If you're a programmer then you'll be glad to hear that the entire project is open source on GitHub, we look forward to your pull requests.
- The itch app is available in over 20 languages, thanks to the itch.io community!

name: Type Off
summary: A short 6 min typing speed game
longDescription:
A short 6 min typing speed game.

Random characters pop up from the left side and move toward the right side of the screen. You lose a life if any character disappears after hitting the right edge. Moreover, you only have three lives. No respawn.

Can you make it to the end?
changelog: The final finished version of Type Off

name: TheGates
summary: Free and open-source 3D internet browser build with Godot Engine
longDescription: Welcome to the new internet! Here, you can explore various worlds created by developers from all over the world! Follow the portals to travel between these worlds and discover the ones that truly captivate you. If you're seeking adventures, then this place is perfect for you!
changelog: Renderer updates now reach existing installs — previously a cached world renderer was never refreshed after download

name: SeriousSamClassic-VK
longDescription:
SeriousSamClassic-VK is open source game engine version developed by Croteam for Serious Sam Classic with Vulkan support, but it should work on (or be easily portable to) any system that supports Vulkan and SDL2.

Note that while the Serious-Engine source code has been released under GPL, you still need to legally own the game and provide Serious Sam Classic The First Encounter and Serious Sam Classic The Second Encounter the game data to play. See the how to install section for more information.
changelog:
Updated release package to SeriousSamClassic-VK 1.10.7

Added borderless mode for all resolutions

Added large font to Netricsa for high resolutions

Added the ability to switch to Legacy Hud

name: SeriousSamClassic
longDescription:
SeriousSamClassic is open source game engine version developed by Croteam for Serious Sam Classic, but it should work on (or be easily portable to) any system that supports OpenGL 1.3 and SDL2.

Note that while the Serious-Engine source code has been released under GPL, you still need to legally own the game and provide Serious Sam Classic The First Encounter and Serious Sam Classic The Second Encounter the game data to play. See the How to Install section for more information.
changelog:
Updated release package to SeriousSamClassic 1.10.7

Added borderless mode for all resolutions

Added large font to Netricsa for high resolutions

Added the ability to switch to Legacy Hud

name: WebP Converter
summary: The fastest way to convert images to WebP
longDescription:
WebP Converter allows you to convert images to the WebP format. It is on average 93% faster than online alternatives, with no limit on amount of converts and ability to control compression quality.

With a compression setting of 60, you will notice minimal reduction in quality while shrinking file size to around 90% of its original size.
changelog:
Features:

- Statistics view: view data on images like how much space was saved
- Image input is now scrollable and allows for drag and drop
- New screenshots to reflect changes

name: Jamulus
longDescription:
The Jamulus software enables musicians to rehearse, play music or perform real-time jam sessions over the internet

This is the build of Jamulus, packaged into a Flatpak.

name: Bugdom
summary: Save Bugdom from Thorax's evil Fire Ants
longDescription:
The Bugdom was once a peaceful place ruled by the Rollie Pollies and the Lady Bugs, but not long ago the Bugdom was overthrown by the clan of the Fire Ants. After recruiting other bugs to help fight for them, they captured all of the Lady Bugs and are holding them prisoner. The leader of the Fire Ants, the new king of the Bugdom, is King Thorax. Once he is defeated, the Bugdom will return to the peaceful place it used to be.

You are Rollie McFly, the only remaining bug capable of saving the Lady Bugs and restoring peace to the Bugdom. Rollie has been hiding in the Lawn area of the Bugdom and will need to travel far to get to the Ant Hill where the battle with King Thorax must take place. There will be water to cross, bugs to ride, and plenty of enemy forces to defeat, but once the Fire Ants and King Thorax have been defeated, you will become the new ruler of the Bugdom and peace will be restored.

About this port: Bugdom was released in 1999 by Pangea Software. It was a pack-in game on Macs that came out around that time. This port aims to provide the best way to experience Bugdom today. This port was made and re-released under permission from Pangea Software, Inc.
changelog:
New in this release:

- Fix framerate-dependent behavior in game physics
- More fitting dark cyclorama in level 9 and 10 intros

name: Bugdom 2
summary: Track down the Bully Bee and get your knapsack back!
longDescription:
It has been three years since Rollie McFly rid the Bugdom of the evil King Thorax and his minions, but the Bugdom can still be dangerous place as our new hero Skip is about to find out. While on his way to visit his family on the far side of the Bugdom, a Bully Bee swooped down and stole Skip’s knapsack. Your job as Skip is to track down the Bully Bee and get your knapsack back. The chase takes place mostly in and around a house.

You will make new friends in the Bugdom who will help you through each area. Keep an eye out for Sam the Snail and Sally the Chipmunk. Sam will usually make you prove your worthiness before he will help you, but Sally is just interested in gathering acorns, so be sure to brings lots of those to her. Additionally, the same Buddy Bugs that helped Rollie McFly defeat King Thorax will help you defeat most mean enemy bugs that you encounter.

About this port: Bugdom 2 was released in 2002 by Pangea Software. This port aims to provide the best way to experience the game today. This port was made and re-released under permission from Pangea Software, Inc.
changelog:
Initial release of the modern version.

Compared to the last Mac release by Pangea, this version introduces the following improvements:

- Widescreen support
- Improved mouse and controller support
- Seamless terrain texturing
- Minor gameplay bugfixes

name: Cro-Mag Rally
summary: The wildest racing game since man invented the wheel!
longDescription:
In Cro-Mag Rally you are a speed-hungry caveman named Brog who races through the Stone, Bronze, and Iron Ages in primitive vehicles such as the Geode Cruiser, Bone Buggy, Logmobile, Trojan Horse, and many others. Brog has at his disposal an arsenal of primitive weaponry ranging from Bone Bombs to Chinese Bottle Rockets and Heat Seeking Homing Pigeons.

In addition to single-player racing where one player races against the computer, there are also several different multi-player modes including Tag, Quest for Fire, and Survival. Up to four players can play on a single computer in split-screen mode.

About this port: CMR was released in 2000 by Pangea Software. It was a pack-in game on Macs that came out around that time. This is a port of the original OS 9 version of the game, made under permission from Pangea Software, Inc.
changelog:
New in this release:

- Improved Italian and Spanish localizations
- You can now rebind the left analog stick and the D-Pad to your heart's content

name: Mighty Mike
summary: High-Powered Action Rescue in a Toy Store Gone Mad!
longDescription:
Toy Mart has closed for the evening. The clerks have long since turned off the cash registers, and the midnight janitor has left. Suddenly the store comes alive as dolls, action figures, and game pieces jump to their feet. Within moments cities are formed: in the Bargain Bin, race tracks become islands of action surrounded by a sea of on-looking toy robots. In the Clown Department thousands of insane clowns initiate a massive pie fight. Throughout all of the departments, life arises...

Suddenly there is a commotion in the Doll Department! One of the cages in the Stuffed Animal Zoo has broken open – hundreds of Fuzzy Bunnies hop out of the cage and scatter. The Fuzzy Bunnies, with their limited intellect, do not realize the danger they are in. The new metropolis of Toy Mart can be a very dangerous place for Fuzzy Bunnies to wander alone, and without help they stand little chance of surviving until morning.

The peaceful inhabitants of the Doll Department cry out for the Fuzzy Bunnies to return...but to no avail. What will they do? What will become of the Fuzzy Bunnies?

“I WILL HELP YOU!” storms a deep, resonant voice from one of the shelves. A hush crawls over the crowd of Fuzzy onlookers. A large package tumbles from the shelf onto the floor and bursts open...and a figure emerges. Yes, it's Mighty Mike – the most powerful action figure money can buy!

About this port: Mighty Mike was initially released as a Mac exclusive under the name “Power Pete” by Pangea Software in 1995. This port aims to provide the best way to experience the game today. This port was made and re-released under permission from Pangea Software, Inc.
changelog:
Changes since version 3.0.1:

- Custom OpenGL-based framebuffer renderer. Better performance and power efficiency than the previous renderer.
- Toggle fullscreen with Alt+Enter
- Stability fixes

name: Nanosaur
summary: Send dinosaur eggs to the future before a meteor hits the Earth!
longDescription:
You are a dinosaur (a Nanosaur to be exact) from the future who has traveled back in time to collect the eggs of 5 dinosaur species before the giant asteroid hits the earth. The “primitive” dinosaurs will attack you as you try to get their eggs, but just remember that it’s for their own good that you blast them into oblivion!

Being a dinosaur from the future, you are equipped with several pieces of technology to help you in your mission:

You can jump, swim, run around, jet around, shoot stuff, etc. The general rule to playing the game is “if it moves, kill it or it’ll kill you.” You only have 20 minutes to collect all 5 egg species so being efficient about your actions is critical.

About this port: Nanosaur was released in 1998 by Pangea Software. It was a pack-in game on Macs that came out around that time. This port aims to provide the best way to experience Nanosaur today. This port was made and re-released under permission from Pangea Software, Inc.

- Fusion Blaster: a multipurpose weapon for killing things.
- Jet Pack: for flying over things that might kill you.
- Temporal Compass: for finding time portals.
- GPS Locator: for figuring out where you are and where you should go.
changelog:
New in this release:

- Fixed physics for very high framerates
- Ironed out problems with first-person camera
- New settings: aspect ratio, sky color, deinonychus dentistry fix
- Pin GPS to upper-right corner of 3D viewport in widescreen mode
- Fix frustum culling inconsistencies
- HiDPI support
- Other stability, performance, and cosmetic fixes

name: Nanosaur 2: Hatchling
summary: Fly a pterodactyl who’s loaded with hi-tech weaponry
longDescription:
In the year 4122, a solo Nanosaur was sent 65,000,000 years into the past. His mission was to find the unhatched eggs of ancient dinosaur species and return them to the future. The mission was a success, but before the eggs could be hatched, they were stolen by a group of rebel Nanosaurs. The rebels took the eggs to offworld bases where they planned on breeding the dinosaurs. Their goal was to create warriors for fighting their battle against Earth.

But the rebels left one egg behind. . . when it hatched, a new Nanosaur was born. This hatchling was sent on a mission to recover the stolen eggs and defeat the rebel forces.

Nanosaur II: Hatchling is a continuation of the original Nanosaur storyline, only this time you get to fly a pterodactyl who’s loaded with hi-tech weaponry. In addition to the three level adventure mode where you blast enemy dinos and save eggs, there are also six two-player levels including racing, capture-the-flag, and battle.

About this port: Nanosaur 2 was released in 2004 by Pangea Software. It was a pack-in game on Macs that came out around that time. This port aims to provide the best way to experience the game today. This port was made and re-released under permission from Pangea Software, Inc.
changelog:
Initial release of the modern version.

Compared to the last Mac release by Pangea, this version introduces the following improvements:

- Improved widescreen support
- Improved mouse and controller support
- Seamless terrain texturing
- Story subtitles
- Revamped menu system
- Customizable status bar scaling
- Minor gameplay bugfixes
- High-resolution story slides

name: Otto Matic
summary: Save the Earth from the clutches of the Giant Brain from Planet X
longDescription:
The year is 1957 and a fleet of flying saucers from Planet X have come to Earth. These saucers are under the control of the evil Brain Aliens who are abducting helpless human beings and taking them away to strange alien worlds to become slaves of The Giant Brain. Luckily for the human race there exist the Otto Matics, robots who police the galaxy in name of all that is good and decent.

You are Otto Matic, the robot who is given the job of saving Earth from the clutches of The Giant Brain from Planet X. You must rescue as many humans as you can while defeating the Brain Aliens and all of their evil followers. Your mission will take you to strange and fantastic alien worlds which are often treacherous and will require Otto to perform amazing feats.

Your rocket ship will take you to each of the planets, starting with Earth. While on each planet you must save as many humans as you can, but be careful because the Brain Aliens will try to abduct the humans before you can save them. When you save humans, they are teleported to your rocket ship. To escape the planet you must also collect rocket fuel. Once The Giant Brain has been defeated and peace restored to the galaxy, you will return to Earth with your human cargo where they will be freed.

In Otto Matic...

About this port: Otto Matic was released in 2001 by Pangea Software. It was a pack-in game on Macs that came out around that time. This port aims to provide the best way to experience the game today. This port was made and re-released under permission from Pangea Software, Inc.

- 10 levels on strange alien planets!
- Battle 25 different alien creatures!
- Attack with 7 different types of space-age weapons
- Fight off giant radioactive killer vegetables!
- Ski behind giant metal beasts on a sea of toxic ooze!
- Ride soap bubbles across noxious lakes of slimy goo!
- Get shot out of a cannon!
- Smash alien clowns in hovercraft bumper-cars!
- Drink radioactive potions to grow to 50ft tall!
- Ride a zip-line to escape mutant radioactive robots!
- Pilot a flying saucer and lay waste to an alien fortress!
- Battle the Giant Brain from Planet X
- And much, much more!
changelog:
Here are the major changes since version 4.0.0 in a nutshell:

- New quality-of-life settings: infobar centering/scaling, camera auto-alignment on/off, etc.
- For completionists: all humans should now be possible to rescue, and the bonus screen will let you know if you've rescued them all
- Physics are more stable, enabling the game to be played at higher framerates
- A lot of polishing: seamless terrain texturing, smooth spline motions, etc.
- Fixed a whole host of minor gameplay bugs and softlocks
- And more!

name: S3Drive
summary: Convert S3, SFTP, WebDAV or Rclone back-end into your encrypted storage
longDescription:
S3Drive is an easy-to-use software client that converts vast range of protocols (S3, WebDav, FTP etc.) and cloud providers into your personal encrypted file storage with comprehensive syncing and backup options.

There are dozens of providers where you can get a free tier account. You can then decide to pay only for additionally used storage or you can fully control your storage by self-hosting S3 or any other back-end.

You can start with the simplest option and make adjustments whenever you're ready. Your files are encrypted before they leave your device, so no one beside you can access them. Not even us.

Features: Rclone compatible E2E encryption, Drive mount, Sync modes (copy, move, sync, two-way), Content and filename encryption, Secure sharing via encrypted link, Multiple accounts support, Manage files & directories (open, preview, download, copy, delete, rename, folder upload etc.), Preview different file formats (pdf, markdown, txt, audio, video), Simple text editor, Search within directories, Object Lock support, File versioning (delete & restore), Light and dark themes

Supported protocols: S3, WebDAV, SFTP, SMB, FTP, HTTP

Personal storage: Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, Box, Microsoft OneDrive, pCloud, Proton Drive, Koofr

S3 clouds: AWS S3, Backblaze B2, Synology C2, Cloudflare R2, Google Cloud Storage, Wasabi, Linode, IDrive e2, Storj, Scaleway, DigitalOcean Spaces

Self-hosted: MinIO, SeaweedFS, GarageFS, Openstack Swift S3, Ceph, Zenko CloudServer

Visit our Docs for full list of supported providers.

Available on: Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, Web

name: Mission Center
longDescription:
Monitor your CPU, Memory, Disk, Network and GPU usage, accompanied by a per app and process breakdown of these statistics

Features:

Limitations (there is ongoing work to overcome all of these):

Comments, suggestions, bug reports and contributions welcome

- Monitor overall or per-thread CPU usage
- See system process, thread, and handle count, uptime, clock speed (base and current), cache sizes
- Monitor RAM and Swap usage
- See a breakdown how the memory is being used by the system
- Monitor Disk utilization and transfer rates
- Monitor network utilization and transfer speeds
- See network interface information such as network card name, connection type (Wi-Fi or Ethernet), wireless speeds and frequency, hardware address, IP address
- Monitor overall GPU usage, video encoder and decoder usage, memory usage and power consumption, powered by the popular NVTOP project
- Monitor system fans
- See a breakdown of resource usage by app and process
- Supports a minified summary view for simple monitoring
- Use hardware accelerated rendering for all the graphs in an effort to reduce CPU and overall resource usage
- Uses GTK4 and Libadwaita
- Written in Rust
- Intel GPU monitoring is only supported for Broadwell and later GPUs; and does not support VRAM, power, or temperature monitoring
- When using Linux Mint/Cinnamon, launched applications may not show up in the "Applications" section (Upstream issue: https://github.com/linuxmint/cinnamon/issues/12015)

name: OpenRCT2

OpenRCT2 is an open-source re-implementation of RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 (RCT2). The gameplay revolves around building and maintaining an amusement park containing attractions, shops and facilities. The player must try to make a profit and maintain a good park reputation whilst keeping the guests happy. OpenRCT2 allows for both scenario and sandbox play. Scenarios require the player to complete a certain objective in a set time limit whilst sandbox allows the player to build a more flexible park with optionally no restrictions or finance.

OpenRCT2 features many changes compared to the original RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 game. A few of them are listed here.

Original RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 or RollerCoaster Tycoon Classic game files are required in order to play OpenRCT2.

- User Interface theming.

- Multiplayer support.
- Multilingual. Improved translations.

- Various fixes and improvements for bugs in the original game.

- Script and live-code with JavaScript, ISF Shaders, Faust, PureData or C++.
- Leverage IoT protocols such as CoAP or MQTT for industrial-grade automation.
- Interact with joysticks, Wiimotes, Leapmotions, Web APIs and BLE sensors.
- Integrate programs from a wealth of creative programming languages such as Structure Synth, Context-Free Art and Bytebeat.
- Load any kind of audio or video format and process visuals through Spout, Syphon, NDI, Shmdata or Sh4lt.
- Use VST3, LV2 audio plug-ins and more.

name: Poezio
summary: Poezio is a free console XMPP client
longDescription:
Poezio is a free console XMPP client (the protocol on which the Jabber IM network is built).

Its goal is to let you connect very easily (no account creation needed) to the network and join various chatrooms, immediately. It tries to look like the most famous IRC clients (weechat, irssi, etc). Many commands are identical and you won’t be lost if you already know these clients. Configuration can be made in a configuration file or directly from the client.

You’ll find the light, fast, geeky and anonymous spirit of IRC while using a powerful, standard and open protocol.

Features

- Encryption: TLS, OMEMO, always chat with encryption.
- Chatrooms: Discuss on your favorite topics with your friends or strangers.
- Carbon copies: Switch devices while staying in the same conversations without losing messages.
- Plugins: Add the features you want through official or other plugins.
- Corrections: Fix your last sent messages.
- Rich text: Send and receive messages with colors and formatting.
- Chat state notifications: See the writing status of your contacts.
- Anonymous: Use XMPP without an account.

Messages, chats, groups and channels stay synced across all your devices, with the client running standalone without needing your phone connected.

name: Obsidian
longDescription:
Obsidian is a powerful knowledge base that works on top of a local folder of plain text Markdown files. In Obsidian, making and following connections is frictionless, and with the connections in place, you can explore all of your knowledge in the interactive graph view. Obsidian supports CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM), along with other useful notetaking features such as tags, LaTeX mathematical expressions, mermaid diagrams, footnotes, internal links and embedding Obsidian notes or external files. Obsidian also has a plugin system with 20+ supported plugins to expand its capabilities.

The documentation can be accessed by opening the demo vault that is shipped in Obsidian.

Obsidian is free for all purposes, including personal, commercial, and non-profit use. No account or license is required for qualifying use cases described in the End User License Agreement. Users have the option to purchase a Catalyst license to get early access to insider builds and support the development. Additionally, Obsidian offers optional paid services for publishing and synchronizing your notes. Details about these optional hosted services can be found on the Obsidian website.

This distribution is verified by the Obsidian team but isn't supported

GPU acceleration can be disabled if necessary by setting OBSIDIAN_DISABLE_GPU=1 in Flatseal

Pdflatex support in pandoc currently requires installing the org.freedesktop.Sdk.Extension.texlive SDK

Note: Regular users should disable "Automatic Updates" within Obsidian as public release updates are handled by Flatpak itself. Insiders should keep this enabled to receive insider builds, as those will not be made available on Flathub.

This flatpak goes into great lengths to provide a nice experience for end users. In order for the Git plugin to work it requires permission to the ssh-auth socket (--socket=ssh-auth). It also exposes the home directory in the sandbox (required for Drag and Drop operations). If you don't use the Git plugin you can disable the ssh-auth socket permission, e.g. using Flatseal. You can also remove access to the home directory if you want and the flatpak will continue to work, albeit with reduced functionality. In case you do remove access to the homedir, note that in order for things to not break for the Git plugin, --persist=.ssh flag has been passed and a bind mount to ~/.var/app/md.obsidian.Obsidian/ is created by flatpak, allowing that location to be used for persistent data (but your home directory's .ssh remains unaccessible)

OpenDeck supports the majority of the original Stream Deck plugins, like Elgato's own Discord plugin, unlike other softwares (e.g. streamdeck-ui, StreamController, Boatswain) which are much more limited.

Please note that you will need to install udev subsystem rules for your device to be detected. For more information, see the Installation section of the project README on GitHub.

Some compiled plugins are not compiled for Linux, so you may need to have Wine (and Wine Mono) installed on your system (natively, as the Wine Flatpak is not supported). Similarly, for using plugins made with Node.js, the Node.js Flatpak is not supported.

From Multi Actions and Toggle Actions to switching profiles when you switch apps and brightness control, OpenDeck has all the features you'd expect from stream controller software.

Consider that the power of your Stream Deck actually comes from the software you use with it, then remember how much you paid for it. To support OpenDeck's development, please consider donating to me on GitHub Sponsors, Ko-fi or Liberapay.

name: Reinschrift
longDescription:
Reinschrift combines a native GNOME interface with the simplicity of plain text. Your tasks remain a normal Markdown file – easy to back up, versionable via Git, and editable on any device with your favorite editor.

The app syncs the file via Nextcloud/WebDAV, reads changes live, writes directly back, and thus makes classic to-do lists in plain text suitable for everyday use – without proprietary silos. The format remains open, portable, and transparent.

name: Deliveries

name: Dynamic Wallpaper
summary: Create light/dark wallpapers for GNOME 42 and beyond
longDescription:
GNOME 42 introduced a dark style preference, and with it, support for combined light/dark wallpaper pairs. Unfortunately, there's no easy way in GNOME to add your own wallpaper pairs—until now!

Dynamic Wallpaper makes it easy to select a wallpaper to use with the default style and a different wallpaper (e.g. a nighttime version) to use with the dark style. Choose a name, save your wallpaper pair, then find it in GNOME Settings → Appearance → Background.
changelog:
New stuff:

Updated all translations to match the new design.

name: Stencil
longDescription:
Stencil is a batch file (and directory) renamer for GNOME. Build a rename queue from stackable operations and preview every result before you commit.

Operations include:

Save your operation queues as presets, import and export them, and undo any rename.

- Number - add a sequential counter
- Set Extension - change, normalize or remove the extension
- Insert Text - add text before, after or at a position
- Find & Replace - literal or regular-expression replacement
- Change Case - lower, upper, title or sentence case
- Trim & Remove - drop characters and clean up whitespace
- Date & Time - prefix or suffix a formatted timestamp
- Music Tags - build names from embedded audio tags (artist, title, album, track number, …) using a token pattern like {track} - {title}
- Folder Name - insert the name of a containing folder, from the immediate parent up to any number of levels

- Added an Image Tags operation that lets you rename image files based on their (EXIF) tags.
